historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR +1.5% vs revenue -3.4% and EPS -5.2%: divergence >30%. Equity barely compounds because Venture pays out ~100% of earnings (80c DPS on 78.7c EPS in FY2025). All trailing CAGRs end at the FY2025 trough (Lifestyle Consumer customer down-cycle, tariff volatility) and start near the FY2022 supply-chain peak, so none is a usable forward rate; the forward path is anchored instead on H1 FY2026 (+7.4% revenue, 2Q +12.5% YoY) and management's 'demand continues to strengthen' commentary.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - lease cash (principal + interest, from FY2019 IFRS 16): FY2019 184.3, FY2020 410.8, FY2021 77.2, FY2022 222.9, FY2023 459.5, FY2024 451.4, FY2025 208.0 (S$m). Interest income is not in OCF so no interest deduction. SBC is immaterial, so owner and reported FCF CAGRs track closely. FCF swings are dominated by working capital (FY2021-22 build, FY2023-24 release), which is why the base year is component-built rather than taken from any single period.

scenario_narratives.base: Venture's two swing axes are AI/data-centre infrastructure demand (Portfolio B, ~69% of revenue) and the product cycle of its key Lifestyle Consumer customer. The base case takes management's 'new shoots taking root' at face value for FY2026 (+9%: H1 +7.4%, 2Q +12.5%) and FY2027 (+8%), then decelerates to 2.5%. Revenue reaches ~S$3.5bn by FY2029, back inside the FY2017-22 range rather than above it. EBITDA margin climbs from 11.05% to its 12% decade median on volume, not price, because Venture has limited pricing power against Fortune-500 OEMs. Growth uses cash: net working capital runs ~25% of incremental revenue. The S$1.15bn net cash is valued at book and its interest is excluded from the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The AI capex supercycle runs through FY2028. Test & Measurement and Networking design wins scale, the H1 FY2026 inventory build converts into 2H shipments, and the Lifestyle Consumer co-developed products launch. Tariff-driven diversification out of China favours Venture's Malaysia/Singapore footprint. Revenue grows 12% in each of FY2026-27 and passes S$4bn by FY2029. Operating leverage restores the FY2018-20 13% EBITDA margin, with capex lifted to 1.4% of revenue for capacity.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI cycle turns in FY2027 and hyperscale capex pauses. Customer concentration bites: the key Lifestyle Consumer customer keeps cutting replacement volumes, and another domain loses a programme to a scale peer (Flex/Jabil/Celestica). US tariffs on Malaysian-sourced electronics (19%) cannot be fully passed through, and part of the S$897m inventory is written down. Revenue grows 5% in FY2026, falls 4% and 2% in FY2027-28, and recovers only slowly. EBITDA margin settles at 10%, below any year in the decade. Falling working capital releases cash in the down years. Interest income is outside the flows, so a lower rate path does not change this value.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Mid-cycle owner-FCF DCF of a high-mix EMS/ODM specialist. The operating business is valued on component-built flows from the FY2025 trough-ish base, with no interest income. The S$1.15bn net cash, quoted equity stakes and associate are added at book or fair value, and the September interim dividend and NCI are deducted. The terminal value is capped at 14x (cyclical); Gordon at 8.5%/2% would be ~15.7x. A single negative half (H1 FY2026 FCF -S$0.9m on an inventory pre-build) is treated as working-capital timing, not a new base.
key_risks_to_valuation: AI/data-centre capex reversal hitting Portfolio B, ~69% of revenue
Single-customer concentration in Lifestyle Consumer and per-domain concentration generally
US tariff policy on Malaysia-sourced electronics vs ~80% Malaysian capacity
S$897m inventory: write-down risk if 2H shipments slip
Terminal value dominance: cap multiple and the 12% mature EBITDA margin drive most of the value
Cash treated as fully excess; if ~S$200-300m is really operating liquidity for an EMS, value falls ~S$0.7-1.0/share

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 287.41m issued ex-treasury at 30 Jun 2026 (H1 FY2026 note 7) plus ~0.6m dilutive share awards (FY2025 EPS note: diluted 288.526m vs basic 287.925m weighted). Held FLAT: SBC (tiny, ~0.07% of revenue) is expensed in the flows; buybacks are value-neutral.
inputs.cash_composition: Cash and cash equivalents S$1,108.484m + short-term investments S$37.482m at 30 Jun 2026. Zero borrowings. Lease liabilities (S$16.2m) EXCLUDED from debt under lease treatment (B).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income was S$39.1m (H1 FY2026 S$13.2m, -36.8% YoY on lower rates), ~14% of PBT. It is NOT in reported FCF: Venture classifies interest received in INVESTING activities and subtracts interest income in the OCF reconciliation, so reported OCF/FCF is already ex-interest. Deducting it again would double-strip; the field is therefore 0. The S$1.15bn cash pile that earns it is added at book in the bridge instead (bridged separately, not capitalised as owner earnings), which makes the valuation independent of the SGD/USD deposit-rate path. Last_fcf = reported FCF 223.474 - SBC 1.724 - lease cash 13.794 (principal 12.811 + interest 0.983, treatment B) = 207.956.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report cash flow statement, 'Share-based payments expense' S$1,724k; no net-share-settlement tax line (EquityAwardTaxes 0 every period). Singapore is an SBC-light market.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 S$18.0m, H1 FY2026 S$5.5m in financing ('payments for shares purchased and cancelled'); the H1 FY2026 presentation cites ~S$46m repurchased to date under the plan (cumulative). Venture is a modest repurchaser, so the flat count is partly funded in cash.
inputs.wacc_rationale: SGD build, no debt so WACC = cost of equity: Singapore 10y SGS ~2.3% + beta ~1.05 x 5.75% mature-market ERP = ~8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Same rate in every scenario: cyclicality, tariff exposure and customer concentration are charged once, in the scenario flows and the 25% bear weight, not as a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: lease principal + interest (S$13.8m FY2025, 0.54% of revenue) charged through lease_cost_pct_path; da_pct_path is PPE depreciation + amortisation only (ex right-of-use, S$21.8m FY2025 = 0.86%), so EBIT for tax is not double-charged; lease liabilities excluded from net debt.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI (S$0.5m/yr profit, S$5.6m book) deducted once in the equity bridge at ~14x earnings.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, scenario-weighted, plus owner-fcf-adaptations (non-US SGD WACC, IFRS-16 leases treatment B, small NCI, matching-asset rule for cash and quoted equities, SBC-near-zero). Routing: Venture is a non-US cyclical operating company (EMS/ODM), not a financial, REIT or holdco; first valuation, no MEMORY entry. FY0 CALIBRATION: FY2025 EBITDA S$280.0m (11.05%) excludes investment revenue; less SBC 1.7, lease cash 13.8, D&A ex-ROU 21.8 gives EBIT ~242.7, x(1-20%) = NOPAT ~194, plus after-tax interest ~31 = ~225 vs reported attributable NPAT 227.0 -- ties. NORMALISATION: H1 FY2026 FCF was -S$0.9m because inventories rose S$201m (S$695.8m -> S$897.0m) to pre-buy materials for H2 shipments. The base year is NOT that half; flows are component-built from FY2025 margins with working capital charged at -25% of the revenue CHANGE (net working capital ~24-28% of revenue). The June 2026 cash anchor already carries the inventory build; the ~S$95m of H1 working-capital investment above the growth-proportional norm (~S$0.33/share) is NOT credited back in any scenario -- a deliberate conservatism that would reverse if 2H converts the inventory as management guides. Cross-check: 7-year (FY2019-25) average owner FCF S$288m vs model base year-10 FCF ~S$300m, so the terminal capitalises a mid-cycle, not peak, level. Interim dividend of 30c (S$86.2m, paid 11 Sep 2026) post-dates the June balance sheet and the stock trades ex it, so it is deducted in the bridge.

bear.narrative: Hyperscale capex pauses in FY2027, US tariffs on Malaysia squeeze pass-through, the key Lifestyle Consumer customer keeps shrinking and part of the H1 inventory build is written down; margin settles at 10%.

base.narrative: AI/data-centre demand carries FY2026-27 (Test & Measurement, Networking & Comms, Semi equipment), Lifestyle Consumer stabilises, revenue regains ~S$3.5bn by FY2029 (still below the FY2017-22 S$3.0-4.0bn range at its top), EBITDA margin recovers to its 12% decade median.

bull.narrative: AI capex supercycle persists; inventory build converts to 2H shipments; Lifestyle Consumer new product cycle ramps; supply-chain shifts out of China favour Malaysia/Singapore. Margin returns to FY2018-20 13% on operating leverage.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% for the documented customer concentration (FY2025's -7.4% came from one customer), the 19% US tariff on Malaysia, where ~80% of capacity sits, and the execution risk in a S$201m inventory build. Bull is cut to 25% because it needs the AI cycle to last, the inventory to convert and Lifestyle Consumer to recover at the same time. The base case keeps 50%. There is no solvency risk: zero debt and S$1.15bn of cash.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
